notRead: any output of other V11 strands
firewall.enforcement: instruction (R4), documented here; this strand's scripts read only the protocol, V10 code/engines, product series via the research loader, SPY, and the private V10 PIT factor panel

priorExposure.statement: The V10 findings over the FULL period are known to this strand and are prior knowledge, not TRAIN evidence.
knownFindings: V10 signal backtest 2000-2025: no SPY excess Holm-significant for the five rules; NEW_52W_HIGH 13w SPY excess declines over subperiods (+5.1% 2000-07 ... -0.7% 2020-25)
V10 pattern evidence: strong-12m-momentum 13w and three-month-thrust 52w beat the contemporaneous base rate

V10 factor reconstruction 2010-2025: small positive rank ICs for momentum (all horizons), profitability and quality (1M/3M); top-quintile spreads not positive; Top-50 composite strategy 13.0% vs SPY 12.3% CAGR, below the equal-weighted survivor population 14.0%
V10 funded NEW_52W_HIGH strategy 2000-2026 CAGR 16.4% vs SPY 5.9% on a survivor cohort, not cost robust
priorExposure.literatureKnown: Momentum (Jegadeesh-Titman 1993), 52-week-high proximity (George-Hwang 2004), low volatility (Ang et al. 2006), gross profitability (Novy-Marx 2013), quality (Asness et al. 2013), smooth/continuous momentum (Grinblatt-Moskowitz 2004; Da-Gurun-Warachka 2014), trend filters (Faber 2007).
possiblyInfluencedDesignChoices: Choice of the rule families momentum / trend stability / 52-week high / profitability / quality is informed by V10 full-period ICs (which include VALIDATION and TEST years) and by literature.
The expectation that concentrated or composite price strategies do not beat SPY after costs is known; the exploration nevertheless reports every variant.
Use of the equal-weighted own universe as the selection-skill benchmark is motivated by the V10 finding that the survivor population itself beats the Top-50 strategy.

population.eligibilityAtDecision: close observed at week j and j+1, listingStart <= date(j), at least 57 weekly closes up to j; no price-level or liquidity filter on split-adjusted closes (an adjusted-price filter would select on future splits)
population.survivorship: All frame series end in 2023 or later: the TRAIN and VALIDATION populations contain no delisted firm at all (conditional on survival to >= 2023). Coverage of SEC 10-K filers 14% (2000), 22% (2010), 48% (2020). Every result states this; SPY comparisons are biased in favour of any rule on this cohort.

PRICE.inputs: weekly split-adjusted closes up to the decision week; SPY for relative strength / beta / market filter

FUND.inputs: V10 PIT factor panel (filed < rank date; month-end rank dates 2010-2025) cut to the lifecycle frame + price features

explorationPlan.TRAINonly: Rules are designed, tuned and selected on TRAIN decisions only (price 2001-2012, fundamental 2011-2016). Every evaluated variant is appended to the exploration log with its exact parameters; the count of variants is reported (garden of forking paths).
stages: S1 single signals and simple rank sums x concentration (10/20/50) at 4-week full rebalancing, equal weight
S2 holding rules on the better S1 signals: rebalance interval, buffer (keep while rank in top x%), let-winners-run with rank/trend exits, market filter, weighting variants
S3 robustness of S2 picks: cost stress, TRAIN sub-halves, walk-forward within TRAIN
explorationPlan.walkForwardWithinTrain: research-validation buildWalkForward/runWalkForward over the TRAIN decision calendar (expanding windows); fit = rank variants on train fold, select = best on validation fold, evaluate = test fold: measures the out-of-sample value of 'pick the best explored variant'
explorationPlan.variantBudget: at most 200 price and 150 fundamental variants

evaluation.execution: decision at week close j, execution at close j+1; the last portfolio of a period is held to the next scheduled rebalance and liquidated there
evaluation.ledger: fast simulator mirroring research-portfolio arithmetic for exploration; research-portfolio.cjs (HISTORICAL_PRICE_SIMULATION, numeraire 1) as official ledger for frozen candidates and final hypotheses with parity check
evaluation.returnBasis: PRICE_RETURN for strategy and every benchmark (total return only exists for 8 titles; not mixed in)
evaluation.investment: fully invested at target weights except where a market filter or exit rule holds cash; cash earns nothing
benchmarks: SPY PRICE_RETURN buy-and-hold on the same sessions, no costs
equal-weighted own eligible universe of the rule (same decisions, same costs)
equal-weighted frame population (same decisions, same costs)
PIT cap-weighted frame population from panel market cap (2010+, same decisions, same costs)
metrics: excess vs each benchmark (weekly mean and CAGR difference)

inference.method: research-validation.inferTemporalBlockMean on the weekly return difference (circular calendar blocks)

evaluation.primaryEndpoint: VALIDATION/TEST: mean weekly return difference strategy (base costs) minus SPY (price), two-sided block-bootstrap p, Holm within the frozen family (<= 12)
secondaryEndpoints: difference vs equal-weighted own universe (selection skill; separate Holm family)
difference vs frame EW and cap-weighted population (descriptive)

finalSelectionRule.statedBefore: VALIDATION outcomes (repeated verbatim in the candidates file)
finalSelectionRule.eligible: VALIDATION point estimates: weekly excess vs SPY > 0 AND vs own-universe EW > 0 AND stress-cost excess vs SPY > 0
finalSelectionRule.ranking: Holm-adjusted p vs SPY within family ascending, then raw p vs own-universe EW ascending
finalSelectionRule.ifFewerThanTwoEligible: add the best-ranked remaining candidate of each family not yet represented (labelled DIAGNOSTIC_NOT_VALIDATED) up to 3 in total, so that TEST measures persistence; such entries are not hypotheses expected to work

oracle.label: ORACLE_LOOKAHEAD
oracle.definition: Top-N by realised forward price return over the holding window, equal weight, same costs, same rebalance interval as the compared rule; horizons 4, 13, 52 weeks; N 10/20/50
oracle.use: upper bound and attribution only; computed for TRAIN before candidates are frozen, for VALIDATION/TEST only after the respective freeze; never a candidate source

attribution: Weekly regression on SPY (alpha/beta); population (EW own universe) vs SPY = size/equal-weight effect; per-decision cross-sectional regression of forward returns on standardised characteristics (momentum, volatility, size where PIT market cap exists, quality, value, growth, profitability) -> characteristic contributions and specific selection; concentration (share of P&L from the top-5 positions); costs; cash/timing.
